:::{#exm-second-order-condition}
#### Classifying stationary points

- $f(\vx) = x_1^2 + x_2^2 - 2 x_1$ has the stationary point $\tp{(1, 0)}$ (@exm-stationary-point),
  and its Hessian is

  $$
  \begin{aligned}
  \matr{H}_f(\vx) &= \sbmat{ 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 } \\
  &= 2 \matr{I}_2,
  \end{aligned}
  $$

  which is positive definite, so $\tp{(1, 0)}$ is a strict local minimizer.
- $f(\vx) = x_1^2 - x_2^2$ has the stationary point $\vzero$
  and Hessian $\sbmat{ 2 & 0 \\ 0 & -2 }$,
  which is not positive definite
  ($\tp{(0, 1)}$ gives $-2$).
  Indeed, $\vzero$ is not a [local minimizer](algebra.qmd#def-local-minimizer) (@exm-first-order-condition).

:::
